reason: Complete HTML full text read (short specification paper; no experiments section, no appendix beyond author list); in scope as a portable skill-asset format plus a trajectory-to-skill / patch / cull self-evolution algorithm; treated under rubric A1 (no quantitative experiments).

paper.title: Swarm Skills: A Portable, Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System Specification for Coordination Engineering
paper.central_claim: A portable specification (Swarm Skills) extending the Anthropic Skills standard with multi-agent semantics, plus a companion self-evolution algorithm that distills trajectories into new Swarm Skills and patches them using Effectiveness/Utilization/Freshness scoring and SIMPLIFY/REBUILD/ROLLBACK governance, lets agent teams self-evolve coordination strategies with zero-adapter cross-agent portability and without human oversight.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: no run receipt is exposed to the worker. Rubric A1 applied: all five E sub-items not_reported (rating 0); no formal result exists in the paper.

materials.notes: Figures 1-4 are caption-only in the text material; the case-study Evolution Record JSON is included in the text.

evidence.quote: multi-agent coordination protocols remain locked within framework-internal code or static configurations, preventing them from being shared across systems or autonomously improved over time
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap.

evidence.quote: a portable specification that extends the Anthropic Skills standard with multi-agent semantics
evidence.support_explanation: Specification contribution.

evidence.quote: a companion self-evolution algorithm that automatically distills successful execution trajectories into new Swarm Skills and continuously patches existing ones based on multi-dimensional scoring (Effectiveness, Utilization, and Freshness), eliminating the need for human-in-the-loop oversight during the refinement process
evidence.support_explanation: Algorithmic contribution and the no-human claim.

evidence.quote: Through an architectural compatibility analysis and a comprehensive qualitative case study
evidence.support_explanation: Only validation offered.

evidence.quote: The primary limitation of this work is the absence of large-scale, quantitative conformance testing across diverse Host Agents
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state no quantitative portability test.

evidence.quote: evaluating the quality of multi-agent coordination lacks standardized benchmarks, making it difficult to rigorously quantify the performance gains provided by the self-evolution algorithm across different domains
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state no quantified gain from self-evolution.

evidence.quote: When a multi-agent session concludes, the nuanced coordination decisions—such as how a complex task was decomposed, which roles were dynamically instantiated, and how conflicts were resolved—are discarded alongside the execution trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Bottleneck statement: coordination experience is not persisted.

evidence.quote: the resulting coordination protocol—the ”who does what and when”—remains an internal data structure of the optimization algorithm
evidence.support_explanation: Claim about workflow-search neighbours (AFlow, GPTSwarm, DyLAN, EvoAgent); not verified against their artifacts.

evidence.quote: employ automated search procedures to discover optimal workflow topologies or augment agent capabilities
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest multi-agent workflow-evolution neighbours, none compared.

evidence.quote: Our analysis of 33 search queries across 9 skill repositories revealed a strong ”revealed preference” for multi-agent capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Demand evidence from skill naming and install counts; says nothing about benefit of evolving protocols.

evidence.quote: Swarm Skills mandates the presence of an evolutions.json file, which serves as the skill’s Evolution Experience
evidence.support_explanation: Persistent evolution store inside the asset.

evidence.quote: This ensures that the base specification files (SKILL.md, roles/, workflow.md) remain untouched, mitigating the risk of catastrophic degradation from a single erroneous patch.
evidence.support_explanation: Append-only patch records; base files not edited by PATCH.

evidence.quote: Its ultimate adoption is governed entirely by the Host Agent’s subsequent selection behavior during the USE stage.
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate skills are staged; admission is by later usage, not a test.

evidence.quote: The algorithm employs Bayesian smoothing with a Beta(1,1) prior to stabilize early-stage evaluations, updating the score based on the outcome of tasks executing the patch.
evidence.support_explanation: Effectiveness is updated from task outcomes; how outcomes are judged is not specified.

evidence.quote: The adoption rate of the patch. If the Host Agent’s Leader consistently ignores an appended instruction,
evidence.support_explanation: Utilization = whether the Leader follows the record, not whether it helps.

evidence.quote: A time-decay factor applying an exponential half-life (e.g., 90 days), ensuring that stale optimizations are gradually deprecated in favor of recent adaptations.
evidence.support_explanation: Expiry by age, independent of correctness.

evidence.quote: falls below a predetermined threshold naturally sink to the bottom of the context window and are eventually ignored by the Host Agent
evidence.support_explanation: Threshold and weights w_E, w_U, w_F are not given.

evidence.quote: Executes an LLM-driven pruning operation on the Evolution Experience, categorizing records for deletion (low score/stale), merging (overlapping intent), refinement (clarity), or retention.
evidence.support_explanation: SIMPLIFY: LLM-driven consolidation.

evidence.quote: The previous version is archived, and the evolutions.json array is cleared.
evidence.support_explanation: REBUILD versions the base skill and resets the record list.

evidence.quote: Provides a fail-safe mechanism to revert a Swarm Skill to any previously archived state following a detrimental REBUILD operation.
evidence.support_explanation: Rollback exists; the trigger for 'detrimental' is not defined.

evidence.quote: triggered automatically when the evolutions.json array exceeds a specified capacity
evidence.support_explanation: Governance runs on capacity rather than measured degradation.

evidence.quote: we conduct a qualitative system walkthrough using a travel-planning-swarm Swarm Skill
evidence.support_explanation: Single task, qualitative.

evidence.quote: The self-evolution algorithm automatically generated an Evolution Record suggesting a structural split to decouple these responsibilities, and submitted it for user approval
evidence.support_explanation: The one demonstrated structural evolution was human-gated, unlike the abstract's no-human claim.

evidence.quote: While the core algorithm described in Section 5 can operate fully autonomously, the JiuwenSwarm deployment exposes an optional human-review step (interactive mode) for structural changes to ensure operational safety and user alignment.
evidence.support_explanation: Autonomy is claimed for the algorithm but the case study ran in interactive mode.

evidence.quote: "effectiveness_score": 0.5, "utilization_rate": 0.0, "freshness_decay": 1.0
evidence.support_explanation: The displayed record carries initial metrics only; no later effect of the patch is shown.

evidence.quote: Ultimately, the more the Swarm Skill is utilized, the stronger and more efficient the agent team becomes.
evidence.support_explanation: Improvement claim without any measurement.

evidence.quote: the architectural alignment with established progressive disclosure mechanics strongly supports the universal portability of the Swarm Skills specification
evidence.support_explanation: Portability argued architecturally; not tested on another Host.

evidence.quote: we demonstrate how Swarm Skills achieves zero-adapter cross-agent portability via progressive disclosure
evidence.support_explanation: Abstract claim stronger than the architectural-analysis evidence.

evidence.quote: while keeping the overall cost strictly within the 20,000 RMB limit
evidence.support_explanation: Task outcome claim in the walkthrough; no plan, costs or verification shown.

evidence.quote: a comprehensive qualitative case study (a 6-role travel planning team)
evidence.support_explanation: One case, 6 roles.

signatures.object: A Swarm Skill directory (SKILL.md frontmatter, roles/, workflow.md, bind.md, evolutions.json): a natural-language multi-agent coordination protocol; baseline = framework-private coordination config or runtime-only planning that is discarded after the session.
signatures.information: Host Agent trajectories with at least two distinct sub-agent roles and cross-agent dependencies; friction patterns and explicit improvement signals (user feedback or agent reflections) from the trace.
signatures.operation: CREATE (LLM distillation of a trajectory into a candidate skill in staging) -> USE (progressive disclosure: descriptions in the Leader's prompt, on-demand read_file of skill body, roles, workflow, bounds, plus applicable evolution records) -> PATCH (trajectory analyzer appends an Evolution Record with context, change directive and E/U/F metrics) -> governance (SIMPLIFY / REBUILD / ROLLBACK when records reach a capacity).
signatures.output: New or patched Swarm Skill assets and archived versions.
signatures.conditions: Host must support read_file and sub-agent spawning; weights w_E, w_U, w_F, score threshold and capacity (example 10) are not specified.
signatures.feedback: Friction analysis by an LLM trajectory analyzer; outcome of later tasks executing the patch (Beta-smoothed Effectiveness); Leader adoption (Utilization); age (Freshness).
signatures.selection_rule: Score S = w_E*E + w_U*U + w_F*F; low-score records sink and are culled; candidate skills adopted by the Leader's later selection.
signatures.selection_data: Later usage of the same skill; no held-out set or counterfactual.
signatures.persistence: Files in the skill directory with archived previous versions (REBUILD) and an append-only evolutions.json.
signatures.later_use: Leader loads the skill and appended records on matching tasks; assets can be copied to another Host.
signatures.claimed_effect: Teams self-evolve coordination, become 'stronger and more efficient' with use; zero-adapter portability.
signatures.failure_boundary: First-run lock-in (acknowledged), hosts lacking recursive read_file or sub-agent spawning, no standardized benchmark.

signatures.object: The static specification (frontmatter kind/teammate_mode/roles[], natural-language body, bind.md bounds) as a host-independent description format.
signatures.information: Host Agent reads only metadata mechanically and loads the rest as natural language.
signatures.operation: Serialize the coordination protocol into Markdown/YAML extending an existing standard so any compliant host executes it with its native tools; non-supporting hosts ignore extra fields and degrade to a single agent.
signatures.failure_boundary: No conformance test on any second host.

gap.author_gap: Multi-agent coordination protocols live in framework-internal code or private configs and are discarded after each session, so they can neither be shared across systems nor improved over time (no 'coordination experience sedimentation').
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and specific for the persistence/portability side; demand evidence (community skill naming, installs) is observational. The claim that neighbouring workflow-optimisation outputs 'remain internal data structures' is stated, not checked, and the benefit of persisting coordination experience is not measured.
gap.lineage: Single-agent skills (Voyager, ExpeL, SAGE, EvoSkills, Anthropic Skills) -> multi-agent workflow search (GPTSwarm, DyLAN, AFlow, EvoAgent) and framework-private formats (CrewAI, MetaGPT SOPs, AutoGen) -> Swarm Skills (portable multi-agent skill + evolution records).
gap.closest_adjacent: Single-agent skill evolution (Voyager/ExpeL/EvoSkills) with the same distill-patch-cull cycle; workflow-search systems that already produce topologies and roles; none compared.
gap.residue: Evidence that persisting and patching coordination protocols improves later tasks, and that the format runs on a second Host.
gap.stakes: Re-planning collaboration from scratch each session; lock-in to frameworks.
gap.method_response: A host-independent skill format with a mandatory evolution-record file plus a CREATE/PATCH/governance algorithm.
gap.remaining_gap: Quantitative portability and gain evidence, a defined effectiveness signal, rollback trigger, first-run lock-in governance, cost.
unresolved: Neighbouring papers (AFlow, GPTSwarm, EvoSkills) not fixed in this batch; whether their outputs are persistable is taken from the paper's statement.

matches.reason: The specification serialises heterogeneous framework-private coordination configs into one shared, host-readable surface form (Markdown/YAML) so any compliant host executes it without adapters, which is the C18 serializer move; the evolution loop itself has no original-card counterpart.

rs_pattern.reason: Parent-level and C18 fit is partial; the self-evolution algorithm is covered by domain cards.

condition_checks.note: SIMPLIFY (delete/merge/refine), REBUILD with archive, ROLLBACK, capacity trigger.
Staging directory and score-based culling exist; no execution test or marginal-gain test before a skill or record is retained.
Friction from traces and user feedback ground patches; the outcome signal behind Effectiveness is unspecified.
No with/without counterfactual for a record; Effectiveness is a smoothed outcome average.
Admission by staged adoption and retirement by score, decay and capacity; no attribution, replay or regression budget.
Versioning, archive and rollback are specified, but the measured admission/retirement test that would drive them is not.
Each record targets named files (e.g. roles/copywriter.md, workflow.md) with a friction context.
Whether the observed friction is caused by the edited role/workflow is not checked.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Serialising a heterogeneous coordination protocol into one shared host-readable format (rs C18) = compiling interaction streams into portable versioned skill packages published for other agents (rsi H02).
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Explicit contract another agent can execute: present. Retention gate by execution/quality, coverage tracking, and reuse evaluation on disjoint tasks/agents: absent.
pattern_mapping.differences: C18 expects an ablation vs the skeptic's baseline and specialist parity; H02 expects downstream reuse gains, not library statistics; neither is provided.

expectations.applies_when: Gain attributed to the shared format.
expectations.reason: No ablation or comparison isolates the format or the evolution mechanism from simply prompting a host with the same text.
No baseline of the same team run from a framework-private config, an ad-hoc prompt, or without evolution records.
Only the JiuwenSwarm reference host is exercised; other hosts only argued.

expectations.applies_when: A foregrounded capability (portability, self-improvement) is claimed.
expectations.reason: No metric for coordination quality, portability conformance or improvement over uses.
E/U/F weights, 90-day half-life, capacity 10 and the append-only choice are not ablated.
A reference implementation and a Skills Hub are named; their contents were not inspected by this reviewer.
Staged candidates and score-based culling, but no execution test or judge-controlled versioned merge before reuse.
No counterfactual contrast; Effectiveness is Beta-smoothed outcomes of tasks that used the patch.
LLM calls for distillation, analysis and SIMPLIFY/REBUILD are not costed.

expectations.applies_when: Patches target an artifact with structure.
expectations.reason: Evolution records name target files and the friction context; attribution quality is untested.
The only structural evolution demonstrated was submitted for user approval and executed after user confirmation.
Who or what judges 'outcome of tasks executing the patch' is undefined; Utilization is adoption, which can reward harmful but followed patches.

claims.text: Swarm Skills achieves zero-adapter cross-agent portability via progressive disclosure.
claims.setting: Architectural analysis plus a walkthrough on the JiuwenSwarm reference host.
claims.result: No cross-host test; authors list conformance testing as the primary limitation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A host-independent file format whose portability follows from reuse of an existing standard (design argument); not empirically established.

claims.text: A companion algorithm lets teams self-evolve coordination protocols without human oversight and become stronger with use.
claims.setting: 6-role travel-planning team on JiuwenSwarm, one run.
claims.result: One Evolution Record proposing a role split, approved by the user and rebuilt; no later-task measurement.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Feasibility of generating a patch record and applying a role split in one interactive run; no evidence of improvement or autonomy.

claims.text: There is demand for shareable multi-agent skills.
claims.setting: 33 queries over 9 community skill repositories, April 2026.
claims.result: Team-named skills and high install counts for adversarial/parallel skills.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Observational evidence that users express multi-role workflows in single-agent skills; motivates the format, not its benefit.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Lowest level used by default: no task or retained-improvement measurement exists, only a feasibility walkthrough.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A concrete file format (SKILL.md + roles/workflow/bind + append-only evolutions.json) and a CREATE/PATCH/SIMPLIFY/REBUILD/ROLLBACK algorithm were specified and one interactive run of the reference implementation produced an Evolution Record and a role split; portability and self-improvement are design claims.
assessment.not_supported: Cross-host portability, improvement with use, autonomy without human review, comparative benefit over framework-private formats or workflow-search systems.

G.reason: A real, specific bottleneck (coordination decisions discarded and locked to frameworks) with community-demand evidence and named neighbours on both the skill-evolution and workflow-search sides, but the claim that neighbours cannot persist their outputs is unchecked and the cost of not persisting coordination is not shown.

M.reason: Mechanism is concrete and sensibly motivated (append-only records protect base files; score, decay and governance control bloat), but the effectiveness signal is undefined, utilization rewards adherence rather than benefit, freshness is age-based, and no distinguishing prediction against simply editing the skill is given.

X.reason: Lifecycle, file layout, progressive disclosure, archive and rollback are described, but weights, thresholds, Effectiveness judge, rollback trigger and candidate-skill admission test are missing, the demonstrated structural change needed human approval, and conflict resolution is delegated to an LLM SIMPLIFY pass.
